content:
Camila Reyes: Hey all — trying to lock the final approval chain + publish date for Northwind. Draft is basically there. Can we confirm who *must* sign off before we merge PR + go live?

Camila Reyes: Current guess:
1) Marketing (me) ✅
2) Product Marketing / messaging (Soojin)
3) Solutions Eng / technical accuracy (Markus/Simran)
4) CS readiness (Rachel)
5) Legal (Michael/Sofia)
6) Customer final approval (Northwind)

Camila Reyes: Target publish: Wed 11/6 (so Sales can use it in Nov pipeline). If legal review stalls, what’s our fallback plan?

Soojin Lee: +1 on that list. I’d add a quick “claims/proof” check as its own gate (but that can be covered by me + Markus).

Soojin Lee: For publish date: 11/6 works. I’m mostly focused on the metrics phrasing + avoiding anything that reads like a guarantee. The reliability/fallback section is the touchiest.

Ethan Wallace: Draft vFinal is here (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/northwind-case-study
Ethan Wallace: Web version is already in the docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/4879

Ethan Wallace: What I need from this thread:
- “go/no-go” list of approvers
- a hard deadline for edits (otherwise I’ll keep getting nits forever :sweat_smile:)

Markus Klein: Technical sign-off: Simran + I can do today EOD.
Markus Klein: Biggest items:
- Dedicated sizing language (don’t imply fixed GPU type)
- routing/fallback: be precise that it’s *policy-based routing* + *compatible model variants* (not magic)
- caching/batching: keep as “configured + tuned” vs “automatic everywhere”

Simran Kaur: I’ll verify the architecture diagram export matches what’s in the PR (diagram block + captions). Also want to double-check we’re not naming internal components.

Rachel Kim: CS sign-off is fine as long as we keep reference load guardrails in place. Northwind has been responsive but I don’t want them getting hammered right after publish.
Rachel Kim: Can we add one line in the internal sales talk track: “Limit to 2 reference calls / month, coordinate via CSM”?

Camila Reyes: Yep, good call. That’s for enablement doc + brief template but I can note it.

Avery Johnson: Customer approval status: we’re waiting on their comms + legal for the *final* page proof. They asked for a 5 business day review window in the email thread.
Avery Johnson: If we want 11/6 live, we need to send them the near-final version by Fri 11/1 latest.

Michael Grant: Legal side: I can review the final copy + placement of logo/quote/attribution once we have:
- exact quotes (final wording)
- the metrics disclaimer block
- any numeric claims flagged (esp. latency + cost)

Michael Grant: Biggest risk is if we include exact numbers without a clear “measurement context” + if they want anonymization.

Sofia Mendes: +1. If Northwind’s legal asks for changes to the consent language, that can take longer than copy edits.
Sofia Mendes: Please don’t merge to public until we have either (a) signed consent or (b) we strip logo/name/quotes and publish as an anonymized “customer story” without attribution.

Tyler Benson: For tracking: I can mark a single “Approval status” field in HubSpot + keep the Slack checklist updated, but I need the decision on fallback path.
Tyler Benson: Options I see:
1) Slip publish date
2) Publish anonymized (no logo, no company name, no direct quotes, ranges only)
3) Keep it “sales-only” PDF in Drive until legal clears

Camila Reyes: Ok, let’s define the fallback explicitly so we don’t debate it at the last second.

Camila Reyes: Proposal:
- Primary path: Publish with full attribution (logo + quotes) on 11/6.
- If customer/legal approval not in by 11/4 EOD: we switch to sales-only PDF + internal enablement, and we hold public publish until approvals land.
- If we *really* need something public (for campaign timing), we can publish an anonymized version, but only with Legal sign-off and no direct quotes.

Soojin Lee: I like “sales-only PDF” as the default fallback. Anonymized case studies tend to underperform and invite skepticism.

Ethan Wallace: Works for me. If we do sales-only PDF fallback, I’ll export a clean 1-pager + put it in the enablement folder.

Markus Klein: One more wrinkle: Support flagged a transient p95 spike during the interview window (SUP-3812). It was resolved, but we should avoid quoting a single-day p95 number.
Markus Klein: Recommendation: publish either (a) a range, or (b) “p95 improved by X% over a 30-day window” if we have that approved.

Simran Kaur: +1 — and add “workload + configuration dependent” line in the metrics footnote.

Camila Reyes: Great catch. Ethan/Soojin can you update the results section to avoid anything that could conflict with the spike ticket?

Ethan Wallace: Yep. I’ll revise “p95 latency to 220ms” type statements into “p95 improved ~30–40% (measured over 30 days)” *pending approval*.
Ethan Wallace: I’ll tag the sentence with a comment in the PR so Legal sees it.

Michael Grant: Thank you. If it’s ranges + measurement window, that’s much easier to defend.

Avery Johnson: On customer review: I can send them the “final proof” PDF + web preview link as soon as we lock copy. Their comms person asked for exact pull quotes in context.

Rachel Kim: Also, please make sure the ask to Northwind includes a reminder: we’ll route all reference requests through me (CSM). That has helped with other accounts.

Camila Reyes: Action items + dates:
- Markus/Simran technical sign-off by today EOD
- Soojin messaging/claims pass by tomorrow noon
- Ethan updates metrics/results language + pushes PR update by tomorrow EOD
- Michael/Sofia legal review starts once PR updated (goal: 48h turnaround)
- Avery sends customer final proof by Fri 11/1

Camila Reyes: Hard edit cutoff on our side: Mon 11/4 12pm PT. After that only critical fixes.

Soojin Lee: :thumbsup: I’ll do the claims pass and drop comments directly in PR-4879.

Markus Klein: :thumbsup: We’ll comment in the PR once the diagram + technical sections are clean.

Simran Kaur: I’ll also sanity-check the “routing/fallback” wording vs the approved messaging pillar language.

Sofia Mendes: Please @ me when the PR is updated. I’ll focus on attribution + consent alignment.

Tyler Benson: I’ll create a simple checklist in the tracking sheet + mirror it in HubSpot notes. Also will note the fallback plan (sales-only PDF).

Camila Reyes: Perfect. Ping me if anything blocks. If legal/customer is trending late by 11/4, we’ll switch to sales-only PDF and keep the web page behind the scenes.

Ethan Wallace: Copy that. Going heads down on edits now.
